title: Contextual Alert Setup with Timeline Snapshots and Runbook Diffs
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design and prototype a new alert-creation experience that surfaces historical timeline snapshots, projected SLO drift, and a compact runbook diff to accelerate on-call handoffs. This flow is intended for the Redwood Console alert setup modal and the alert detail page. The objective is to reduce misconfigured alerts, shorten handoff noise, and make postmortem links and remediation suggestions visible at the moment of alert configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Alert creation modal includes a collapsible "Timeline Snapshot" showing last 30d incidents and SLO trajectory
SLO projection mini-graph updates in realtime when threshold/aggregation changes
Runbook Diff panel shows explicit recent runbook edits and highlights recommended snippets for handoffs
On-call Handoff snippet generator can produce a 3-line summary and attach postmortem link automatically
Prototype tested in design review with PM & ENG and receives explicit sign-off or a prioritized list of changes
design_notes: Key UX gamble: show predictive SLO drift inline rather than behind an analytics page — tradeoff is added cognitive load in the modal; mitigations: collapsible sections and contextual defaults

Data layering: timeline snapshot should default to high-level events (incidents, escalations, major config changes) with an option to expand to raw traces — requires event tagging from ENG telemetry team
Runbook diff sourced from Docs drive; if a runbook is missing, offer templated snippets based on alert type (latency/error-rate/cost spike)
Cost-awareness: when an alert uses high-cardinality aggregations, show expected query cost badge (approx tokens / compute) and a suggested lower-cost aggregation alternative
Accessibility: ensure graphs have text alternatives and keyboard navigation for the diff and snippet composer
decisions: Keep timeline snapshot collapsed by default to reduce modal height; surface a single-row incident summary inline
Implement SLO projection as a simplified 7/30/90-day view, not a full forecasting engine for MVP
Use templated runbook snippets for unknown runbooks; do not block alert creation if Docs integration fails
Expose a "cost badge" computed by the backend instead of estimating entirely in frontend
review_comments: PM (Anika Morales): Prefer the 7-day projection default for high-volume services; add a toggle to view 30/90 day to avoid noise
Eng (Ravi Singh): Backend needs new event index endpoints for the timeline snapshot; dependency added ENG-1842. Also flagged rate-limiting for runbook content fetches.
SRE (Jordan Lee): Suggest adding a quick "rollback alert" action in the handoff snippet if the service has a canary rollout pattern
Design review (Leah Ortiz): Visual hierarchy good; request stronger affordance for copying handoff snippet and one-click attach of postmortem link
